question.problem: The function $x(t)$ models the number of meters traveled by a car, $t$ seconds after it sets off on a journey. What is the best interpretation of ${x}^{′}(30)=10?$
question.worked_solution:
The function ${x}^{′}(t)$ represents the rate at which the number of meters is changing at the moment $t$ seconds after starting its journey.

Therefore, ${x}^{′}(30)=10$ means:

$\,$ *$30$ seconds after the start of the journey, the distance traveled increased at a rate of $10$ meters per second*
